# officelens

> Offline accessibility audit for DOCX and PPTX.

officelens opens a Word (`.docx`) or PowerPoint (`.pptx`) file, reads the OOXML package directly, and reports the structure that blocks assistive technology: missing alt text, heading order, document language, table headers, and link text, across the main part, headers, footers, and notes. It also ships a typed library and a browser playground that audits files locally.

It runs entirely offline, with no network calls, no telemetry, no JVM, and no GUI. Output is human-readable text, stable JSON (one object for a single input, an array for many), and SARIF 2.1.0 for code scanning. Exit codes are `0` (clean), `1` (findings at or above `--fail-on`), `2` (invalid usage or a package that is not valid OOXML), and `3` (I/O error).

## Docs
- [Overview](https://officelens-srivtx.vercel.app/): Offline DOCX and PPTX accessibility audit, with an in-browser playground.
- [Rules](https://officelens-srivtx.vercel.app/rules): Every DOCX and PPTX rule code and how the audit reads OOXML parts.
- [Usage](https://officelens-srivtx.vercel.app/usage): Install, CLI flags, exit codes, JSON output, and the TypeScript library API.
- [CI](https://officelens-srivtx.vercel.app/ci): SARIF 2.1.0 output for GitHub code scanning and an exit-code gate for pull requests.
- [FAQ](https://officelens-srivtx.vercel.app/faq): Scope, limitations, and comparisons to the Microsoft Accessibility Checker, Accessr, and schema validators.

## Optional
- [Source](https://github.com/srivtx/officelens): TypeScript implementation, tests, and issue tracker.
- [Install script](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/srivtx/officelens/main/install.sh): One-line install of the `officelens` binary.
